data.title: Modi draws US chip leaders’ backing
data.description:
CHIPPING IN: Micron plans to assemble hundreds of millions of chips in India next year, while Applied Materials is to invest US$5bn in the country over the next decade

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi yesterday launched a charm offensive for global investors at India’s top chip-industry event, drawing pledges from US firms Applied Materials Inc and Lam Research Corp for billions of dollars in outlays.

Marking India’s audacious bid to win a seat at the global chipmaking table, Modi touted the country’s vast pool of engineering graduates and semiconductor-friendly policies as assets international companies should take advantage of.

“The world urgently needs new and reliable locations for manufacturing,” Modi told the conference in New Delhi. “India is readying itself constantly.”

Modi is using the three-day Semicon event to display India’s fledgling chip and electronics industry that barely existed a decade ago. He is courting global semiconductor producers, potential partners and customers for India’s homegrown contenders, as well as equipment makers and parts suppliers all seeking to ride the artificial intelligence investment wave.

The stakes are high for an economy that has outpaced much of the world for years. Modi is trying to prove the nation has what it takes to become a hub in higher value-added industries such as chips, all part of a bid to further modernize the economy and keep it humming by bolstering exports. Expanding manufacturing is crucial for Modi’s vision of moving more workers from farms into better-paying jobs.

“Semicon in New Delhi is Modi’s way of signaling that India has a long-term commitment to growing the chip industry,” said Pranay Kotasthane, deputy director of Bangalore-based think tank Takshashila Institution. “That’s his message to global investors.”

More than 600 exhibitors, more than 150 speakers and 300 global companies are converging on a state-of-the-art convention center in New Delhi. There are to be start-up showcases and a student hackathon.

The event comes just two months after India pledged a further 1.9 trillion rupees (US$19.86 billion) in subsidies to boost local chip and electronics production. The first round of subsidies in 2020 and 2021 helped Apple Inc expand iPhone manufacturing in the South Asian region. It now makes 25 percent of its marquee device there.

India sought to replicate that momentum in semiconductors with an initial US$10 billion fund that helped drive early initiatives. Some of those are starting to bear fruit.

Conglomerates Tata Group and Murugappa Group have begun packaging and assembling chips, while US memory maker Micron Technology Inc has also commenced production. Tata is also building a chip fabrication plant in western Gujarat that is due to become operational in early 2028.

Executives from Micron and Tata spoke ahead of Modi, pledging to forge ahead with their local plans.

Micron plans to test and assemble hundreds of millions of chips in India next year after starting output from its Gujarat plant this year, chief executive officer Sanjay Mehrotra said.

Chip-equipment maker Applied Materials is to invest US$5 billion in India over the next decade, said Prabu Raja, president of the US company’s semiconductor products group.

Competitor Lam Research plans to invest about US$1 billion in a local manufacturing facility, chief operating officer Sesha Varadarajan told the audience.

Germany’s Infineon Technologies AG, known for power and automotive chips, boosted its workforce 28 percent in the country over the past year, chief executive officer Jochen Hanebeck said.

Countries around the world are committing massive budgets to making chips at home as the race for AI supremacy heats up. AI is already becoming ubiquitous in everything from self-driving vehicles and healthcare to finance and fraud detection.

However, as computing resources remain scarce, chips and chipmakers are fast becoming kingmakers in deciding who is winning.

Although India’s push is in early stages, it is accelerating efforts to build a domestic industry spanning the entire supply chain. It is offering seed funding to start-ups working on semiconductor products, support for chip-making gear as well as for new fabs and assembly plants.

data.title: Winbond shares rise on news of Infineon deal
data.description:
‘SPANSION’: The portfolio of products tailored for automotive, industrial and infrastructure markets was expected to strengthen Winbound’s market position

Shares of Winbond Electronics Corp (華邦電), the world’s leading NOR flash memory maker, edged up 0.59 percent yesterday, paring a 6 percent intraday rally triggered by its announcement of a US$1.12 billion acquisition of Infineon Technologies AG’s NOR Flash and F-RAM portfolio.

The acquisition comes as the memorychip industry undergoes a supercycle, driven by a supply crunch that Winbond estimated could last through 2028.

Winbond shares closed up at NT$170 yesterday, the highest in four trading days. The deal is expected to solidify its global leadership in NOR flash memory and deepen its penetration into the automotive sector.

About 28 percent of the chipmaker’s memorychip revenue last quarter came from the automotive and industrial segment. Winbond last year had about a 23 percent share of the global NOR flash memory market, data compiled by Omdia showed.

The portfolio Winbond is acquiring is NOR Flash and F-RAM products tailored for automotive, industrial and infrastructure markets, Infineon said.

The deal would help bolster Winbond’s research and development efforts and supply chain resilience, as well as enhance customer services, the Kaohsiung-based memory chipmaker said in a statement on Wednesday.

The company plans to operate the portfolio as a standalone entity with headquarters in Silicon Valley, it said.

The new entity would use the legacy “Spansion” name, marking the return of a historical brand to the memorychip industry, Winbond chairman Arthur Chiao (焦佑鈞) said in the statement.

Winbond and Infineon aim to close the transaction in the second half of next year. The deal remains subject to regulatory approval.

Spansion Inc was a California-based memory maker that in 2015 merged with Cypress Semiconductor, which was acquired by Infineon in 2020. Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD) and Fujitsu Ltd founded the company in 1993 as Fujitsu AMD Semiconductor Ltd before AMD took full control of the company and renamed it Spansion in 2004.

data.title: Citi supports Taiwanese companies’ growth in central and eastern Europe amid supply-chain shifts
data.description:
Amid ongoing shifts in global supply chains, Taiwanese companies are increasingly seeking to diversify their operations, move closer to customers and strengthen their presence in key overseas markets. Citi is drawing on its global network and on-the-ground capabilities to help clients assess opportunities and navigate their expansion in Central and Eastern Europe, including Poland, Citi Country Officer for Poland Elzbieta Czetwertynska said on Monday in Taipei.

She told a small group of Taiwanese reporters that the needs of Taiwanese companies in the region span across multiple industries.

Citi supports clients by providing local market insights and solutions tailored to their cross-border business needs.

A strategic gateway to Europe

The trend reflects the growing importance of “near-shoring” and “friend-shoring,” as companies seek to reduce exposure to geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions by locating production closer to major markets or in countries regarded as strategic partners.

Poland is particularly well positioned because of its location between Western Europe and the wider Central and Eastern European region, Czetwertynska said. Poland’s economy is approaching the US$1 trillion milestone and progressing toward developed market status. GDP growth is projected at approximately 3.5-3.6 percent this year, around three times the EU average, she said.

Its established industrial base and skilled workforce could complement Taiwan’s strength in technology and hardware manufacturing.

Trade and investment ties deepen

The relationship is also being reinforced by rapidly growing trade. Bilateral trade exceeded US$2.5 billion in 2025, according to Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs, with integrated circuits, semiconductors and LCD panels accounting for about 60 percent of Poland’s imports from Taiwan.

Polish imports of computers, servers and electronic components from Taiwan surged about 500 percent in the first half of 2026 from a year earlier, underscoring the growing role of AI and data-center investment in the bilateral relationship.

Green energy transition, supply chain security and digitalization are among the key investment themes, Czetwertynska said.

AI infrastructure offers opportunities

AI infrastructure is likely to be one of the most promising areas. Taiwanese companies involved in AI servers, GPU systems, server racks, power supplies, liquid cooling, thermal management, networking and data-center power systems could use Poland as a production or service base for the European market.

The opportunity is not limited to final assembly. Taiwanese companies could also establish local operations in testing and packaging, equipment maintenance, precision machinery, automation, vacuum systems, factory infrastructure and semiconductor equipment components, Czetwertynska said.

Poland’s automotive industry offers another potential entry point, providing Taiwanese suppliers with a base from which to serve European automakers and parts manufacturers, she said.

Green energy transition could create opportunities in battery-management systems, power electronics, inverters and energy-management systems as Poland expands renewable power, energy storage and grid infrastructure.

Beyond manufacturing

Another emerging area is drones. Poland accounted for nearly 60 percent of Taiwan’s drone exports in 2025, making it Taiwan’s largest export market for the products. The two markets could deepen cooperation by combining Poland’s system-integration capabilities with Taiwan’s strengths in key drone components, Czetwertynska said.

Poland as a regional platform

The potential extends beyond Poland itself. Its position within the EU means companies establishing operations there can use the country as a base for serving customers across the bloc, while Poland’s proximity to Ukraine could also become strategically important when reconstruction begins.

The reconstruction of Ukraine could eventually generate more than US$500 billion in economic opportunities, with Poland expected to play an important role as a regional gateway.

For Taiwanese companies, however, establishing a European base also means navigating a more complex regulatory environment, Czetwertynska said. A factory in Poland is likely to serve customers across the EU, exposing companies to requirements involving carbon emissions, supply-chain transparency, sustainability and other regulations.

The longer-term opportunity, Czetwertynska said, is therefore not simply to use Poland as a lower-cost production location, but to build a deeper presence that connects Taiwanese technology supply chains with European industrial markets.

Taiwanese companies are increasingly moving beyond exports toward local manufacturing, research and development, industry partnerships and joint ventures.

Citi’s role

Citi has supported clients through changing market environments. With a presence in over 90 markets, Citi helps clients capture cross-border opportunities around the world, said Christie Chang, Citi Country Officer for Taiwan and Chairman of Citibank Taiwan Ltd.

Through close collaboration between its Taiwan and Poland teams, Citi helps companies expand into the European and Central and Eastern European (CEE) markets.

Citi provides insights on the local investment environment, macroeconomic developments, and geopolitical trends, while offering cross-border banking solutions including trade finance, supply chain finance, foreign exchange, cash management, and corporate financing.

Through the One Citi model, clients benefit from a consistent and seamless banking experience across different markets.

data.title: Wiwynn expects major increase in Texas production
data.description:
Server manufacturer Wiwynn Corp (緯穎科技) yesterday said its US capacity would make up about 20 percent of the company’s total production capacity next year, after a new line in Texas enters volume production in the second quarter of next year.

The plant in Socorro, Texas, would mainly focus on rack-scale server production for general-purpose servers and servers based on application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), a company official said.

Wiwynn, which has invested US$1.6 billion into the El Paso County site, made the remarks after holding an opening ceremony on Tuesday.

Construction of the first building began last year and the facility started mass production in the first quarter of this year, the company said.

A second building is to begin production in the second quarter of next year, Wiwynn said.

“The opening of our Texas facility marks an important extension of Wiwynn’s global manufacturing footprint and a key step in strengthening our supply chain resilience,” Wiwynn chairwoman Emily Hong (洪麗甯) said in a statement.

“This site will provide advanced production capacity for server racks, becoming a vital hub for Wiwynn’s artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure business in the US,” she said.

Mexico accounts for 70 percent of Wiwynn’s total production capacity, followed by Malaysia at 20 percent and Europe at 10 percent, the company official said.

After the second building in Texas enters mass production next year, US capacity is expected to account for 20 percent of the company’s total capacity, they added.

General-purpose servers accounted for the majority of Wiwynn’s server shipments in the first half of this year, but ASIC-based servers would catch up this quarter and make up half of the total shipments and to surpass general-purpose servers next quarter, they said.

Wiwynn would also begin shipments of graphics processing unit-based servers by the end of next quarter, they said.

While supplies of key components, including central processing units and memory, remain tight, Wiwynn’s inventory is at a healthy level, the official said.

The company introduced a procurement agency model for memory chips mainly used in general-purpose servers to mitigate risks, with chip costs borne by those customers, they said.

Wiwynn’s business outlook for the second half and the whole of this year remains unchanged, as it expects sequential and annual growth driven by robust demand for AI servers.

data.title: NDC approves Longtan Science Park expansion
data.description:
The National Development Council (NDC) yesterday approved a plan to expand Taoyuan’s Longtan Science Park (龍潭科學園區) by 104 hectares, a project expected to create about 4,500 jobs.

The NDC, the policy planning arm of the Executive Yuan, approved the plan submitted by the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) at a review meeting.

The plan next goes to the Executive Yuan for final approval.

The expansion is intended to enhance the semiconductor industry cluster in the Taoyuan-Hsinchu-Miaoli area and further consolidate Taiwan’s competitive advantage in the high-tech sector, the NDC said in a statement.

The NT$95.63 billion (US$2.99 billion) expansion project would be funded through annual budget allocations from the Science Park Bureau’s Operation Fund, it said.

Under the plan, reviews of development permits for nonurban land and an environmental impact assessment are to be completed by the end of 2028.

Following land acquisition, the design and construction of park infrastructure would begin in 2030, with companies allowed to build their facilities concurrently, the NDC said.

The NSTC and Taoyuan City Government selected the 104-hectare site on the eastern side of Longtan Science Park in response to the growing demands of semiconductor firms, it said.

Once the expansion is completed, companies at the site are expected to produce NT$550 billion of goods and services per year and create about 4,500 well-paying jobs, it said.

Longtan Science Park is one of six satellite parks overseen by the Hsinchu Science Park (新竹科學園區).

The Longtan site currently covers 106.94 hectares and employs about 7,000 people, mainly in the integrated circuit, optoelectronics and biotechnology sectors, the Hsinchu Science Park’s Web site says.

In May, local media reported that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (台積電) was seeking government approval to build an advanced wafer fab at Longtan Science Park following the expansion.

data.title: Meta launches Meta One subscription service in Taiwan
data.description:
Meta Platforms Inc on Tuesday announced the official launch of Meta One in Taiwan, a subscription service bundling premium features, artificial intelligence (AI) usage quotas and advanced creative tools across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp.

Single-product plans start at NT$49 per month for WhatsApp Plus, and NT$69 each for Instagram Plus and Facebook Plus, the company said in a statement.

Cross-platform Core plans begin at NT$159, and Premium plans begin at NT$519 per month, Meta said.

Plans tailored for creators and businesses range from NT$369 up to NT$8,999 for the top-tier option, or NT$11,400 via in-app purchase, it said.

The service, targeting individual power users, creators and small businesses, has attracted more than 15 million subscribers and trial users globally, Meta said.

The initial rollout includes more than 50 features, while the core functions of Meta’s platforms would remain free, it said.

The company is introducing subscriptions to provide more professional tools and AI capabilities for users who need them, while maintaining its advertising-supported free services, Meta vice president of Subscriptions Helen Ma (馬海倫) told an online briefing.

Subscriptions would also help Meta establish a more stable recurring revenue stream beyond digital advertising, Ma said, adding that the service could assist small businesses through AI agents within Meta's ecosystem.

Meta has no plans to introduce a paid ad-free option, Ma said, adding that the company remains committed to its free, ad-supported model.

data.title: SK Hynix mulling making chips in US
data.description:
APPEAL: Any agreement to produce advanced memory such as HBM or DRAM could run into opposition from Seoul as those technologies are sensitive, sources said

South Korea’s SK Hynix Inc is in talks with Intel Corp about a deal that would see it manufacture memory chips on US soil for the first time, three people familiar with the discussions said.

Under one potential scenario, SK Hynix would lease part of Intel’s long-planned chipmaking facility in Ohio, they said. Under another scenario, it could form a venture with Intel and major cloud firms that are keen to lock in memory supplies, two of the people said.

A deal would relieve pressure on Intel, which has been struggling, and mark a big win for US President Donald Trump’s administration, which has been ramping up pressure on chipmakers to build in the US as relentless investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers fuels an acute shortage of memory chips.

However, potential opposition from Seoul could be a major hurdle, the sources said.

One of the sources described the talks as exploratory and stressed that no decisions have been made, adding that SK Hynix might consider other ways to structure the deal.

SK Hynix’s product lineup includes DRAM chips used in servers, PCs and smartphones and NAND flash memory chips that provide long-term storage memory. It is also the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI processing units.

Any agreement to produce advanced memory such as HBM or even DRAM could run into opposition from the South Korean government as those technologies are considered sensitive, said the three sources who declined to be identified as the information is not public.

SK Hynix said in a statement that it is “reviewing various measures, including establishing additional production bases, to strengthen the competitiveness of its memory business,” but “no matters have been determined at this stage.”

Intel declined to comment on what it called speculation, but added that it was continuing with investments in Ohio to ready the site.

Asked about a potential SK Hynix plan to produce chips in the US, South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said any decision would be at the company’s discretion, but if it involved a “national core technology,” it would be subject to a review under the Industrial Technology Protection Act.

The US Department of Commerce did not respond to a request for comment.

Manufacturing semiconductors in the US costs much more than in South Korea, the sources said.

Building in the US entails significantly higher labor and construction costs, and much of the semiconductor industry’s supply chain is located within Asia, which also increases US costs, one of them said.

Even so, SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won said in July that the company faces enormous pressure and lobbying from customers and countries to supply more chips.

“I think we need to build a factory in the United States. If possible, I believe we should build it,” he told reporters.

data.title: Global power grid to struggle, TrendForce says
data.description:
Despite rapid growth in data center power demand, global grid capacity has failed to keep pace, market researcher TrendForce Corp (集邦科技) said yesterday.

Global data center power demand is forecast to grow 31 percent to 161 gigawatts (GW) this year from 122.9GW last year, and further increase by more than 30 percent to 211.1GW next year, the Taipei-based researcher said in a statement.

TrendForce attributed the growth to rising power demand from general servers, artificial intelligence servers, other information technology equipment, and non-information technology equipment such as cooling and power supply systems.

The researcher said grid deliverability was sufficient to meet growing data center power demand through last year, but supply and demand began to diverge this year, with the gap expected to widen markedly after 2028, it said.

By 2030, global data center power demand is forecast to reach 490.7GW, while grid capacity available to data centers would total 222.6GW, it said.

Assuming all other electricity demand is fully met, the gap would still total 268GW, it added.

In the US, where data center deployments are the largest, operators’ self-built power supplies and existing facilities are expected to meet a significant share of demand through 2028, TrendForce said.

This would allow most grid-scheduled projects to be energized on time, it said.

However, grid-delivery delays are expected to become more pronounced from 2028, widening the gap between data center power supply and demand, it added.

data.title: Taiwan shares close higher, but turnover still low
data.description:
Taiwanese shares closed higher yesterday, but turnover remained low as investors stayed cautious ahead of a US Federal Reserve policy decision due later in the day, with high expectations of a rate hike.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) closed unchanged at NT$2,380. The stock, which went ex-dividend yesterday, returned to its pre-ex-dividend price within 27 minutes of the market opening.

The quick recovery indicated investor confidence in the outlook for TSMC, a major beneficiary of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, despite investor concern about the possibility of a rate hike by the Fed.

The optimism over AI-related demand also supported shares of memory suppliers and some electronic component makers, with Nanya Technology Corp (南亞科技) rising 5.96 percent and Winbond Electronics Corp (華邦電子) gaining 5.96 percent.

The TAIEX ended up 337.41 points, or 0.74 percent, at 45,848.9. However, turnover of NT$643.7 billion (US$20.19 billion) was below the average of NT$689 billion over the previous five sessions, Taiwan Stock Exchange data showed.

“Today’s gains were technical in nature as the TAIEX rebounded from losses in the past few sessions,” Hua Nan Securities Co (華南永昌證券) analyst Kevin Su (蘇俊宏) said.

Over the previous four sessions, the TAIEX had fallen 1,671.87 points, or 3.54 percent.

“But investors showed little interest in chasing prices as many of them awaited the Fed’s decision and signals about its next move,” Su said, adding that investors were focused on comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the Fed’s dot plot, which shows policymakers’ projections for interest rates.

There is widespread expectation that the Fed would hike rates for the first time in three years as inflation remains elevated in the US and above the Fed’s 2 percent target.

“Today, financial stocks moved higher on hopes that a rate hike by the Fed will boost their overseas interest income,” Su said.

Cathay Financial Holding Co (國泰金控) gained 2.27 percent and Fubon Financial Holding Co (富邦金控) rose 1.32 percent yesterday.

“Taiwan’s central bank will make its [monetary] decision [on] Thursday afternoon,” Su said. “If the central bank follows its foreign counterparts in raising rates, the TAIEX could be affected.”
